review_text:

It's loud talk, low yell kind of loud, at least in the upper area where we were. Seriously... My wife and I joked that this is a good place for married couples but not for a date because there is no chance of having any kind of conversation across the table. And that is despite being almost elbow to elbow with the next table.

Food was very good and the service was attentive and friendly.

Restaurants like higher sound levels as it makes it seem more "alive".

WHY IS THE MUSIC SO LOUD!!!!?

I like music.  In fact, I love music.  I play music. I go to music events.  I have accepted that no restaurant can tolerate, or thinks its customers can tolerate, a quiet background.  So, there's music. But this was so loud it made me feel anxious and rush my meal. Is that what restaurant management wants?  There's no need in this case, because it wasn't at all crowded, I could have lingered and relaxed without a tiny bit of guilt over making others wait for a table.  But yet I couldn't, because it was too loud.

Great place for a casual evening on a quiet block near Rittenhouse!

review_text: We made a 7:00p Tuesday night reservation recently and were seated promptly upon our arrival.  Initially the restaurant was quiet but by 7:45 the place was packed. Entrees: Pork with peanut sauce, Drunken Noodles with Shrimp and Scallops with Spinach were all excellent.  The restaurant has an interesting variety of Thai and Fusion entrees.
